value.rationale: SlowMo is designed specifically to combine infrequent synchronization with persistent slow momentum, and the number of local steps is a central communication hyperparameter. The theorem exposes a sharp and unexpected parity effect: slow momentum can rescue fast steps beyond the ordinary scalar SGD stability limit only for odd synchronization periods, while even periods receive no stability extension at all when alpha is one. This distinguishes the stabilization supplied by persistent slow momentum from the interpolation-only Lookahead slice and provides a concrete boundary for communication-period tuning.
